Nora G: Morning 0% brain dump: we've been debating whether to ship a tiny cross-language contracts package (headers, metric keys, enums) or to publish a versioned negotiation endpoint that SDKs call to learn the schema. I'm leaning toward the package for speed, but want to call out operational tradeoffs.

Luca T: Package wins for developer ergonomics. Platform pushing a new header is painful if every SDK needs a bespoke patch. Single package means: one changelog, one QA pass, faster hotfixes.

Priya S: True but package means we become responsible for releasing across PyPI, npm, and Go module proxies. That CI is doable but we need clear owner and runbooks for emergency patches.

Derek M: The negotiation endpoint model is appealing for dynamic experiments (A/B header sets by region) but adds runtime dependency and increases surface area for fault tolerance. If the endpoint goes flaky, SDKs need solid offline defaults.

Nora G: Exactly. Also want to avoid the SDKs shipping divergent header normalizers. If each SDK implements the mapping, we get subtle bugs (casing, prefixing, tag names). The central package mitigates that.

Priya S: Implementation suggestion: keep package intentionally tiny. Only export: header names, metric keys, route_policy enum, quota_bucket enum, and helper funcs: normalize_headers(), parse_contract_version(). Nothing more. No retry logic, no HTTP clients.

ops-bot: infra-bot: scheduled: contracts-prototype CI run at 2026-03-24T09:00Z (run-id: prot-7191).

Luca T: For distribution: we can build on top of GitHub Actions matrix to produce artifacts and then auto-publish to private registries first (internal npm/org PyPI). Public publishing can be gated. That reduces risk for early rollouts.

Devex Sam: Console rollout notes: need mapping UI that gracefully shows unknown route_policy IDs. UX: show numeric id, fallback label "Unknown policy", and a small tooltip: "New policy rolled out on DD/MM, enable mapping in Console -> Contracts to see friendly name". Also provide a CSV export for customers to map IDs to billing centers.

Derek M: Telemetry: decide canonical metric names now. Suggest `infra.redwood.quota.requested_tokens` and `infra.redwood.quota.assigned_tenant`. Also tag `route_policy` and `sdk_version`. Publish these as consts in package so dashboards can reference them without string-literals.

Priya S: Go consumers will be a pain: some teams vendor dependencies and rarely update. Add console-level opt-in: "auto-accept-contract-updates" so platform can route older clients safely for a while. That buys us time for library updates.

Nora G: Rollout plan proposal: 1) land contracts package repo with triage owners 2) CI cross-build + publish to internal registries 3) SDKs add dev-dep and run integration tests in CI matrix 4) console add mapping fallback and opt-in toggle 5) enable feature flag in platform -> monitor metrics named `contracts.adoption.*`.

Luca T: Tests: build an integration harness that runs the same header normalization assertions against py/ts/go artifacts. Failing test should block publishing. Put it in GH actions matrix and require green before merge to main.

Devex Sam: Telemetry events we should emit: `contracts.published`, `sdk.imported_contract_version`, and `console.mapping_enabled`. That lets us correlate adoption timelines with any quota or routing anomalies.

Derek M: Edge-case: if platform changes route fallback semantics (cost vs latency) that's an observable behavior change. Mark that as a major version bump for the contracts package and require an explicit changelog entry plus 2-week notice for enterprise customers.

Priya S: Security: ensure the package does not bake in secrets or endpoints. It should be pure constants + pure functions. Any network call remains platform responsibility.

Nora G: Action items:
- Nora/Luca to create infra/contracts repo skeleton (this week)
- Priya to draft release & emergency patch runbook
- Derek to author telemetry metric names and sample dashboards for the Console team
- Devex Sam to prototype unknown-policy UI and CSV export mockups
- All: review CI matrix plan (GH actions) and sign-off on required test cases

Luca T: I'll open the GH repo and add initial CI workflow. Will include a minimal example of importing the package in python-sdk and ts-sdk to prove dev-dep path.

Priya S: +1. Let's aim for a short sync after repo skeleton is up. Also flagging that we need legal review if any of this gets published publicly.

Nora G: Thanks everyone. I'll schedule a 20m sync Friday after lunch and drop a rough design doc in the repo. :thumbsup:
